$comment: SYNAPSE -- highest-ever committed value for every ratcheted threshold (E1.8; R2.10, R7.4, R7.8).
scripts/audit/ratchet_truth.py (task 4.3) reads this file with encoding='utf-8' (E-S13-07) and enforces two clauses:
1. MONOTONICITY (R7.4): a committed value on the wrong side of `bound` FAILs naming the threshold id, the
recorded bound (previous), and the committed value (proposed). `direction: up` means bound is the
highest-ever committed value and a lower commit is a regression; `direction: down` means bound is the
lowest-ever committed value (a ceiling that only tightens) and a higher commit is a regression.
2. CONFIG AGREEMENT (R7.8): `guard_constant.value` must equal `shipped.value`. A ratchet constant that sits
below the configuration it claims to guard lets a real regression PASS -- that is the Stryker 26-vs-50
hole this file makes visible. `agrees_with_shipped: false` records the hole; it does not excuse it.
I-7: `measured_at: null` with `status: unmeasured` means NO measurement exists. It is never a pass, and a
fabricated number is never substituted for it (CF-3). Only a run that measured the value may write
Seeded entirely from values already committed in the repo. Nothing here was invented; every entry names its
source file and, where one exists, the symbol that guards it.

negative-control-seed-sets.note: ADR-055 D6 / R6.15. direction: up because MORE independent seed sets is strictly more statistical power -- lowering this below 20 weakens the negative control, so 20 is a floor. Chosen so the expected number of false positives at alpha = 0.05 is exactly 1, the smallest count at which a false-positive RATE is estimable rather than merely bounded. status: unmeasured is correct and not a defect: this is a PRE-REGISTERED design parameter, not an observation, and no run has yet exercised it. Only a run that measured something may write measured_at + source_run (I-7, CF-3).

negative-control-rate-tolerance.note: ADR-055 D6 / R6.15. direction: down because this is a CEILING on the proportion of negative-control repetitions allowed to report a proven gain -- raising it would weaken the gate, so it may only tighten. Deliberately loose against the nominal alpha = 0.05: at 20 repetitions the exact binomial upper bound on an alpha = 0.05 process is 4/20 = 0.20 at roughly the 98th percentile, so a correctly-calibrated instrument passes almost always while an instrument reporting gains on a third of its null repetitions fails. Tightening to 0.05 itself would fail a CORRECT instrument roughly a quarter of the time -- a gate that punishes the truth. status: unmeasured because this is a pre-registered target, not a measurement.
negative-control-rate-tolerance.$note_on_absent_siblings: The two regret WEIGHTS (regret-weight-shortage = 8.0, regret-weight-holding = 1.0) are PINNED in doc-number-pins.yaml but deliberately carry NO ratchet entry. A ratchet asserts a monotonic better-direction, and for an objective weight neither direction is better -- 8.0 is not 'safer' than 9.0, it is the newsvendor critical ratio this repository already commits in agents/inventory_sentinel/models/newsvendor.py::cost_under. Inventing a `direction` for them would be exactly the fabrication this file's own header forbids ('Nothing here was invented'). They are guarded by their pins and by C75, which verifies each extractor resolves by running it. Recorded here so their absence reads as a decision rather than an oversight. CONTRAST with materiality-margin-service-points below, which DOES carry a direction: unlike a weight, a falsification threshold has an obvious self-serving sign.

materiality-margin-service-points.note: ADR-055 D2.5 / R5.2. The one chosen input to the materiality margin's pre-registered derivation rule: margin = service_points * 0.01 * weight(unmet_service), so at the committed weight of 8.0 this is 5 service points = 0.40 objective units. direction: down because RAISING the margin is the self-serving move -- a larger margin makes `material` harder to reach, which makes Finding 4 harder to falsify, which lets the spec proceed. It may therefore only ever be tightened. This is the one threshold in the phase where the motivated error has an obvious sign, which is why it carries a direction while the objective weights beside it do not. Bracketed on both sides rather than asserted: below ~3.3 points it would call the incumbent (s,S) policy's known shortfall against its own newsvendor target (0.8556 measured vs 8/9 targeted) 'material', and above the measured comparator headroom of 8.86 objective units it would be unfalsifiable by construction. status: unmeasured because the rule is pre-registered before checkpoint A, not observed; only the DERIVED VALUE is instantiated afterwards, by task 10.4, which adds its own pin in the same commit.

stryker-break.note: R7.8 hole CLOSED by task 12.1. The config shipped 50 from Sprint 13 Phase 4.1 (json-canonical.ts reached a 96.30% kill rate) while THREE mirrors of that number stayed at 26: verify_claims.py::STRYKER_BREAK_NOW, CLAUDE.md:46, and this entry's guard_constant.value. Frozen at 26 the gate accepted any config value >= 26, so a silent regression from the shipped 50 down to 26 PASSED C16 -- a gate comparing against a stale mirror cannot catch a regression to it. All three now read 50, which STRENGTHENS the gate rather than raising a ratchet: the enforced floor is frontend/stryker.conf.json and it is unchanged. hard_floor STRYKER_BREAK_MIN stays 20 (the never-below-this bound, deliberately not moved with the ratchet). Next destinations 70 -> 85 per CLAUDE.md's <15%-survival rule; move all three mirrors in the same commit as the config, never ahead of it.

mutation-survival:rewards.note: A ceiling: survival must stay at or below it, so the ratchet direction is DOWN and raising the number is the regression. measured_at is null because mutation.yml runs on a schedule and no survival measurement is committed in-repo (CI-only workload, I-0).

mutation-survival:audit.note: CLAUDE.md states the rewards/guardrails/audit trio as "<15% rewards, <10% guardrails/audit"; the audit leg shares the guardrails number and is recorded separately so a divergence between the two labels is visible.

mutation-survival:audit-chain-walk.note: Task 12.2 added orchestrator/audit/chain_walk.py to mutation.yml under the <10% audit ceiling and deliberately did NOT author this entry: agrees_with_shipped is validated by RUNNING the extractor, and an unverified regex would be a guess with a gate attached (I-7). Authored and verified here in task 12.1 -- `ratchet_truth --check` resolves the extractor against the shipped workflow and reports this row SKIP (declared, unmeasured) rather than UNAVAILABLE (unreadable). The label is `audit/chain-walk`, not `audit`: the sibling `mutation-survival:audit` extracts with `--label "audit"` including the closing quote, so the two regexes each match exactly one site. Without this row ratchet_truth enforced nothing on the new ceiling -- it enforces the entries present, not the converse, so the shipped 10 could later be raised to 40 without failing. measured_at is null for the same reason as its siblings: mutation.yml runs on a schedule and commits no survival measurement (CI-only workload, I-0).

uplift-noise-tolerance.note: R2.6 negative control. The band a null measurement must fall inside: with the Consensus_Arm replaced by a copy of the Baseline_Arm the two arms are identical, so the headline uplift must sit within this many percentage points of zero. A ceiling, so the ratchet direction is DOWN and widening it is the regression -- widening is exactly how a real null-uplift failure would be made to pass. Read by tests/uplift/test_uplift_null_arm_property.py (Property 16), which must never hardcode it; the live value is uplift/cli.py::NOISE_TOLERANCE_PP and this row binds the two together (R7.8 config agreement). status is unmeasured because 1.0 pp is a DECLARED reproduction tolerance, not a measured noise distribution: measuring one means a MIN_POWERED_REPLICATES (1000) run of identical arms, which is .github/workflows/uplift.yml's job and is forbidden on the dev box (I-0). A small-replicate run cannot bound the noise, so no measured_at is invented for it (I-7).

dead-modules-baseline.note: A ceiling on the DEAD set: 0 after the liveness sweep (3 routers wired, 6 orphans removed), so any new orphan is a regression. Task 8.11 landed R13.9's named baseline: infrastructure/quality/dead-modules.yaml is now the sole source and scripts/audit/module_liveness.py::DEAD_BASELINE is derived from it as len(dormant). guard_constant is therefore null -- there is no longer an independent in-code constant to disagree with the shipped value, so recording one would assert a fact the tree contradicts (R7.8 has nothing left to catch here, which is the point). measured_at is null because no committed run record names the sweep.
